rubric.why: Identifies the information as confidential business knowledge.
rubric.description: States that a trade secret is confidential business information.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying it as confidential information belonging to a business.

rubric.why: Explains why the information is kept secret or what value it provides.
rubric.description: Explains that it provides an advantage and is kept from competitors or the public.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for mentioning its advantage or protection from disclosure.

modelAnswer: A trade secret is confidential business information that gives a business an advantage over its competitors.
It is kept secret from competitors and the public.

items.followUp: What is the purpose of a communication protocol?

rubric.why: A protocol specifies rules for communication.
rubric.description: States that a protocol is a set of rules.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying it as rules governing communication.

rubric.description: Connects the rules to communication or data exchange between devices.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the rules govern communication or data exchange.

modelAnswer: A protocol is a set of rules for data communication between devices.
It specifies how data is transmitted and received.

items.followUp: Name one wired and one wireless transmission medium.

rubric.why: States the medium's basic role in communication.
rubric.description: Says that the transmission medium carries or transmits data.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing its data-carrying function.

rubric.why: Identifies the endpoints between which the data travels.
rubric.description: States that it carries data from the sender to the receiver.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming the sender and receiver, or equivalent endpoints.

modelAnswer: A transmission medium is the path or channel that carries data signals.
It transfers data from the sender to the receiver.

items.followUp: How many bits are in an IPv4 address, and how is it commonly written?

rubric.why: The length is a defining property of an IPv4 address.
rubric.description: States that an IPv4 address is 32 bits long.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for giving the correct address length.

rubric.why: Describes the standard representation of the address.
rubric.description: States that it is divided into four 8-bit parts and commonly written in dotted-decimal form.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the four-part dotted-decimal representation.

modelAnswer: An IPv4 address is a 32-bit address used to identify a device on a network.
It is divided into four 8-bit parts and commonly written in dotted-decimal form, for example, 192.168.1.1.

items.followUp: What protocol is commonly used to receive email from a mail server?

rubric.why: Identifies SMTP's main role in sending mail.
rubric.description: States that SMTP is used to send email.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing its email-sending function.

rubric.why: Indicates where or in which direction SMTP handles email.
rubric.description: States that SMTP transfers outgoing email to or between mail servers.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for mentioning outgoing email or its transfer to/between mail servers.

modelAnswer: Simple Mail Transfer Protocol (SMTP) is used to send outgoing email.
It transfers email from a sender's device to a mail server and between mail servers.

items.followUp: What information can be placed in the body section of an HTML page?

rubric.why: Identifies the HTML section being described.
rubric.description: States that the head section is enclosed by the <head> and </head> tags.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the head section or its tags.

rubric.why: Gives examples of information stored in the head.
rubric.description: Names information such as the page title, metadata, styles, or scripts.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming at least one appropriate type of head information.

modelAnswer: The head section is the part of an HTML page enclosed by the <head> and </head> tags.
It contains information about the page, such as its title and metadata, and may include styles or scripts; this information is generally not displayed as the page's main content.

items.followUp: Write a simple HTML anchor that links to https://example.com.

rubric.description: States that an anchor creates a hyperlink.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying that an anchor creates a link.

rubric.why: Identifies the HTML mechanism used to specify the link destination.
rubric.description: Mentions the <a> tag and its href attribute for linking to another page or location.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for mentioning the anchor tag or href attribute and its linking function.

modelAnswer: An anchor is used to create a hyperlink to another web page, file, or location.
The <a> tag uses its href attribute to specify the link's destination.

items.followUp: Explain time and space efficiency and give an example of an efficient algorithm.

rubric.why: Defines efficiency in terms of resources consumed by an algorithm.
rubric.description: Defines algorithm efficiency as the resources an algorithm uses to solve a problem.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for linking efficiency to resource use.

rubric.why: Identifies time as a resource used to assess efficiency.
rubric.description: Mentions the time taken or number of operations as a measure of efficiency.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying time or operations as a measure.

rubric.why: Identifies memory as another resource used to assess efficiency.
rubric.description: Mentions the memory or space used by the algorithm.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying memory or space use.

rubric.why: Gives a concrete comparison demonstrating algorithm efficiency.
rubric.description: Uses the sum of the first 100 numbers to compare a loop with the formula and explains that the formula needs fewer operations.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a relevant example showing why one method uses fewer operations or less time.

modelAnswer: Algorithm efficiency describes how many computer resources an algorithm uses to solve a problem.
It is commonly considered in terms of execution time and memory space.
For example, a loop can find the sum of the first 100 numbers by adding the numbers one by one, requiring 100 additions.
Using the formula n(n + 1)/2 gives 100 × 101 / 2 = 5050 with fewer operations, so this method is more time-efficient for this example.
